newsitem.title: CHILE: Reed boat sets sail from Chile's Easter Island.
newsitem.headline: Reed boat sets sail from Chile's Easter Island.

text.p: A Spanish adventurer has set sail in a reed boat to cross the South Pacific from the remote Easter Island, over a week after the voyage was delayed by bad weather, naval authorities said on Tuesday.

The boat, the Mata Rangi, was launched from a beach on Easter Island on Monday. A successor to the legendary Kon-Tiki, the fragile ship was less than 100 nautical miles from the island by Tuesday, said authorities.

The 11-strong crew was "very enthusiastic and pleased with the successful start to this adventure which they expect to last for six months," said naval commander Ricardo Menzel, quoted in local news media.
The vessel, captained by Spanish adventurer Kitin Munoz, was drifting very slowly at just between three and four knots, he said.
Munoz plans to sail the 100-foot (30 metres) long craft, touted as a replica of primitive ships used before the arrival of Europeans on Easter Island, to New Zealand via Samoa.
But the historical accuracy of the voyage has been questioned by Chilean experts, who said the ship's design bears no resemblance to any ship used by ancient Polynesians.

Others have said the voyage is also based on discredited premises that the island, known for its massive stone moai statues, received cultural influences from the western Pacific thousands of miles away.

With a multinational crew and a message of peace and brotherhood, the project won funding from the Chilean government, the Spanish royal family, the U.N. Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation and various companies.
Spanish Prince Felipe, son of King Juan Carlos who is patron of the voyage, came to Easter Island last month for the launch, which has delayed by bad weather and last-minute technical problems.
Munoz said in Tahiti last month that he considered himself the "spiritual son of Thor Heyerdahl," who sailed from Peru to Easter Island in 1947 in an epic voyage on a balsa raft known as Kon-Tiki.
